pages.title: File:Saigon -- Vue du pont des Messageries.jpg

ObjectName.value: Saigon -- Vue du pont des Messageries

ImageDescription.value: Vue du pont des Messageries, aujourd'hui appelé pont Mong (Cau Mong), construit pour le compte des Messageries maritimes. Wikipédia et d'autres sites mentionnent que ce pont aurait été construit en 1893-1894 ; l'Association des Descendants de Gustave Eiffel donne elle la date de 1882, ce qui semble plus cohérent avec le reste de l'album dont les photos semblent dater des années 1880.
Vue des quais de la gare de Saigon ; il s'agit probablement de la gare qui se trouvait sur l'ancienne place Eugène Cuniac (cf. carte).

ImageDescription.value: Ho Chi Minh City Museum of Fine Arts
Night in Saigon
SONY DSC
Quartier de la Gare

These guys are kickin around a shuttlecock-like toy. As I was watching them a little girl came up to sell me one and at first I refused as I didn't recognise what she was selling. The another little girl approached and when I realised what she was peddling I bought one for $2.

The first little girl came back and started a sob story about how she had to eat. I shared my sob story of how I'm unemployed and I don't need two freakin shuttlecocks. :) She didn't seem to understand, repeating the phrase "buy from me??". It is a phrase I would hear at least a thousand more times in my 11 days in Vietnam.

Artist.value: Yun Huang Yong from Harbord, Australia

Lianas begin life on the forest floor where only receives only 1 percent to 2 percent of available sunlight. But they are much more clever than your average photosynthetic friends; instead of building their own structures, they wind their way up those or other trees, knitting intricate webs between trunks and branches. This method is so effective that sometimes these vines out-complete their host, gathering more light than big tree! -Information board in Côn Đảo National Park-
